units.text: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network. It serves files from locations closer to your users. Those locations are called edges. The origin is where the original content lives. Here, a store keeps its original product photo in an Amazon S3 bucket in North America. A shopper in Asia opens the product page, and CloudFront directs the photo request to an edge suited to serve it.

If that edge already has a usable copy, it can send the photo back on the short path. That is a cache hit. If it does not have a usable copy, that is a miss. CloudFront checks upstream and, if needed, fetches the photo from the S3 origin. It returns the photo and can keep a copy for later requests. CloudFront handles delivery. Protecting direct access to the origin is a separate choice.
